what: Universal Health Services runs about 30 acute care hospitals and roughly 330 behavioural health facilities in the United States and Britain, treating both physical and psychiatric conditions.
customers: Patients and their insurers, plus Medicare, Medicaid and the National Health Service in Britain.
money: general hospitals, mostly in Nevada, Texas, California and Florida
a large part and the better margin
moat: Behavioural health capacity is scarce everywhere and new facilities face long approval processes, so its 330 facilities face little new competition.
risks: Hospital labour costs, especially nursing, have risen faster than reimbursement
Several states have been reviewing provider taxes that fund Medicaid payments to hospitals
opportunities: 7.3 times earnings and 9 times free cash flow with $1.1B of free cash flow
Revenue grew from $12.6B to $17.4B in four years with an 8.6% net margin
Behavioural health demand keeps growing and that segment earns the best margins in the company
watch: Same-facility admissions and the behavioural health operating margin.
